transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m having trouble keeping up when people are talking to me. Like at the museum, someone will be telling me about the next art walk, and I’m looking right at them, but then I realize I missed a chunk of what they said. I end up asking them to say it again.
Do you think you’re having trouble hearing what people say?
I don’t think it’s my hearing, exactly. It’s more like… they’re talking right to me, and I’m looking at them, but then I realize I missed the middle part and have to ask them to run it by me again.
When this happens, does your mind drift off to something else while the person is still talking?

Yeah… I guess it does, in a way. They’ll be talking right to me, like about the next art walk at the museum, and I’m looking at them, but then I realize I missed the middle part. Then I have to ask them to say it again.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks, like reading or finishing things, even when no one is talking to you?

Yeah… sometimes. If I’m reading a gallery packet or notes, I’ll start off okay, but after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still going over the words and I’m not really taking it in. Then I have to go back and read the same part again.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when people talked to you as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t remember every detail, but even in grade school my report cards would say things like “daydreams” or “needs reminders to finish work.” My mother used to sit with me during homework to keep me on track, before I was twelve.
Do you often have trouble understanding what other people mean in conversation, like sarcasm or hints?
Not really… I mean, I think I usually understand what people mean. Sarcasm or hints don’t stand out as a problem for me, at least not that I’ve noticed.
When you miss parts of what someone is saying, is it usually because you’re worried they might judge you?

No… I don’t think it’s about being judged. It’s more like, at the museum, someone will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them, but then I realize I missed a chunk of what they said. Then I have to ask them to say it again.
Do you often have to turn up the TV or phone volume higher than other people prefer?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed needing it louder than other people, anyway.
